clue.text: Is scared to play titular Shakespearean character

indicators.note: letters put into play are moved about freely, so the preceding words are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A nervous actor is frightened of taking the title role in a Shakespeare play.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's play Troilus and Cressida names her in its title, so she is a titular character of the Bard.

clue.text: Texture, say, of cooked duck and game King overlooks

indicators.note: in a down entry, something that overlooks sits above, so the king comes first

parts.note: CR is Carolus Rex, King Charles
I spy is a children's guessing game

explanation.surface: Describing roast duck and game birds, with a king passing judgment.
explanation.definitionFit: Crispy duck is a familiar Chinese restaurant dish, its skin being crisp in texture; 'say' marks this as one example.

clue.text: Fancy beer revolutionary British soldiers gulped down

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so the beer is read backwards

parts.note: ale is beer
B is short for British
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers
ate is past tense of eat

explanation.surface: British troops knock back a fancy beer from a radical brewer.
explanation.definitionFit: Fancy as an adjective means ornate and intricate, as elaborate does.

clue.text: Mandarin in a loose jacket, easily removed?

definitions.text: Mandarin in a loose jacket, easily removed?

parts.words: Mandarin in a loose jacket, easily removed?
parts.note: surface reading: a Chinese official in a baggy coat he can slip off

parts.words: Mandarin in a loose jacket, easily removed?
parts.note: setter's reading: a small citrus fruit whose peel comes away easily

explanation.walkthrough: 'Mandarin' suggests an official, but it is the citrus fruit, and the jacket is its skin.
explanation.definitionFit: The satsuma is a variety of mandarin orange noted for its loose, easily peeled rind.

clue.text: Remained with German newspaper that is to disappear

indicators.note: what disappears is gone, so those letters are removed from the paper's name

parts.note: Die Welt is a German daily
i.e. is id est, that is

explanation.surface: A German paper is set to close, but somebody stays on.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell is to linger or stay, so dwelt is the past tense matching remained.

clue.text: Sorry continent gets 50 per cent reduced funding

indicators.note: cut by half, so only the first half of the continent's name is kept

parts.note: the continent
aid is money given as support

explanation.surface: A sad continent sees its financial aid cut in half.
explanation.definitionFit: As in 'I'm afraid I can't', the word expresses polite regret, just like sorry.

clue.text: Company receiving attention? Maybe it's automatic

indicators.note: to receive something is to take it in, so attention goes inside the company

parts.note: a firm is a company
to give someone your ear is to pay attention

explanation.surface: A firm gets noticed and wonders if it is on autopilot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Automatic' reads as a reflex, but here it is a self-loading gun.
explanation.definitionFit: An automatic is a self-loading gun, one kind of weapon; 'maybe' marks the example.

clue.text: Walk better without frame

indicators.note: a frame is the edging around something, so the first and last letters are stripped

parts.note: one who bets

explanation.surface: Someone recovering from injury walks better without a walking frame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' looks like improved, but it is a person who bets.
explanation.definitionFit: To amble is to walk at a slow, relaxed pace.

clue.text: Doctors keeping smaller, but not large, kitchen furniture

indicators.note: to keep is to hold within, so the doctors wrap around the reduced word

parts.note: Drs is the abbreviation for doctors

indicators.note: but not means excluding, so the letter for large is dropped

parts.note: lesser means smaller
L is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Doctors keep their kitchen furniture small rather than large.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctors' looks like a verb, but it is a plain plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A dresser is a sideboard with shelves for displaying crockery, a classic piece of kitchen furniture.

clue.text: Number will stop female getting raise

indicators.note: to stop a hole is to plug it, so the number fills the middle of the female

parts.note: a hen is a female bird
a number

explanation.surface: A number will block a woman from receiving a pay rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raise' sounds like a pay rise, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To heighten is to make higher or more intense, the same as to raise.

clue.text: Despotic ruler is evil, their banter staggering

indicators.note: something staggering lurches unsteadily, so these letters are knocked out of order

parts.note: the fodder, all fifteen letters

explanation.surface: A tyrant is wicked, and the banter of his court is shocking.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole answer is Ivan the Terrible.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan IV, the first Tsar of Russia, was notorious for cruel autocratic rule, a despot by any standard.

clue.text: Work for almost zero payment ultimately

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the word for zero goes

parts.note: pro means in favour of
a duck is a score of zero in cricket

indicators.note: ultimately points at the very end, so only the last letter of payment is used

parts.note: the last letter of payment

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about working for next to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batter out without scoring has made a duck, hence zero.
explanation.definitionFit: A product is something made, the output or result of labour, as a work is.

clue.text: Sheep, perhaps those looking to cross river

indicators.note: to cross something is to go across it, so the river letter is laid across and inside the onlookers

parts.note: people who gaze
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Sheep, or onlookers waiting to cross a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheep feed on grass in a field, and animals that browse pasture that way are grazers; 'perhaps' marks sheep as just one example.

clue.text: Gross type of celebrity, one believing destiny's inevitable

parts.note: gross in the sense of obese
an A-list celebrity is of the top rank

explanation.surface: A vulgar sort of star who believes in fate.
explanation.definitionFit: A fatalist holds that events are fixed in advance and cannot be changed, so whatever will be, will be.

clue.text: State of flooring inside villa is so regularly ignored

indicators.note: inside means within, so the flooring goes into the kept letters
ignoring at regular intervals drops every other letter and keeps the rest

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters
lino is linoleum floor covering

explanation.surface: The condition of the flooring in a villa is so often overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like condition, but it is a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Illinois is one of the fifty states of the USA, home to Chicago.

clue.text: Great PM at one time

definitions.meaning: second meaning: John ..., UK Prime Minister 1990 to 1997

explanation.walkthrough: PM is the Prime Minister; John Major led Britain's Conservative government in the 1990s.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective for something important or large, and also the surname of a former British Prime Minister.

clue.text: Young animals Julie, not quite seven, trained

indicators.note: training reshapes, so the letters are rearranged
not quite all, so the name loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Julie, not yet seven years old, has been taught to handle young animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A juvenile is an animal not yet fully grown, so young animals are juveniles.

clue.text: Skinful essentially before Oscars I suspect causes drowsiness

indicators.note: before means ahead of, so that letter leads the rest
the essence of a thing is its core, so only the central letter is kept

parts.note: the middle letter of the seven

indicators.note: suspect means dubious, so the letters are not to be trusted in their order

parts.note: the fodder

explanation.surface: Drinking heavily before the Oscars leaves a guest sleepy.
explanation.walkthrough: A skinful is British slang for enough alcohol to get drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Narcosis is a state of stupor or sleepiness induced by drugs, so drowsiness.

clue.text: Notice record temperature, becoming expert

parts.note: an ad is a notice in a paper
an EP is an extended-play record
T is the symbol for temperature

explanation.surface: Someone spots a record temperature and turns into a weather specialist.
explanation.definitionFit: Adept and expert are synonyms: both describe someone highly skilled at something.

clue.text: Shoe one racehorse needs?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the person who prepares a horse for racing

explanation.walkthrough: Racehorses wear shoes too, which makes the two halves seem one idea.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a soft sports shoe, a sneaker, and a person who coaches horses or athletes.

clue.text: Band on the radio yearn to introduce swing

indicators.note: to introduce something is to come before it, so the first part leads and the second follows

parts.note: to long is to yearn
to wave is to swing to and fro

explanation.surface: A wish to bring swing music to the airwaves, as if a band played on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' looks like a group of musicians but it is a frequency band.
explanation.definitionFit: Long wave is a range of radio frequencies used for broadcasting, so it is a waveband on the radio.

clue.text: Military wife right to wear uniform

parts.note: W is short for wife

indicators.note: what is worn goes around you, so the uniform wraps round the letter for right

parts.note: alike means uniform, all the same
R is short for right

explanation.surface: An army wife rightly puts on uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uniform' suggests clothing, but it is the adjective meaning identical.
explanation.definitionFit: Warlike means relating to or ready for war, as military does.

clue.text: Repeated phrase informant rashly employs

indicators.note: to employ is to have on hand, so the answer is carried within the next words

parts.note: spans the end of informant and the start of rashly

explanation.surface: A careless informer uses a stock phrase over and over.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantra is a word or slogan chanted or said again and again, as in meditation.

clue.text: Mad panic gripping old reservists and army officer

indicators.note: to grip is to hold firmly inside, so the reservists sit within the jumble
mad means out of its mind, so the letters of the following word are jumbled

parts.note: the fodder
the TA was the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve, now renamed

explanation.surface: Panic breaks out among old reservists and an army officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A captain is a commissioned army rank above lieutenant, so an army officer.

clue.text: Why it's said informal speaker returns for celebration

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the speaker word is read backwards

parts.note: trap is slang for mouth

indicators.note: said points to how a word sounds when spoken, not how it is written

parts.note: the letter Y sounds like the word why

explanation.surface: Someone asks why a casual speaker comes back for the party.
explanation.definitionFit: A party is a social gathering held to celebrate something.

clue.text: Swimmer from country husband visits each year

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside, so the country and husband enter the per-year term

parts.note: p.a. is per annum, Latin for each year
the country
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A swimmer from abroad whose husband comes to visit every year.
explanation.definitionFit: A piranha is a flesh-eating South American fish, and any fish is a swimmer in crossword terms.

clue.text: Irreligious old man Harry upset

parts.note: pa is father

indicators.note: upset in a down entry means turned upside down, so the word is reversed

parts.note: to harry is to nag

explanation.surface: An unbelieving father called Harry is upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like a name, but it is the verb meaning pester.
explanation.definitionFit: Pagan describes someone outside the main world religions, so not religious in the conventional sense.

clue.text: Shy person using psychiatrist, not half making bloomer

parts.note: shrink is slang for psychiatrist

indicators.note: not half means one half is dropped, here the first three letters of the following word

parts.note: the word to be halved
a bloomer is a flower, and the violet is one

explanation.surface: A timid person sees a psychiatrist, but only half makes a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' suggests a blunder, but it means something that blooms. The whole answer is shrinking violet.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrinking violet is an idiom for a very bashful, retiring person, like the small flower hiding in the grass.

clue.text: Author for instance with hesitant remarks

parts.note: say, as in 'take, say, apples'
er is a hesitant noise, so several are ers

explanation.surface: An author, for example, who speaks with a lot of hesitation.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorothy L. Sayers was an English writer of detective novels featuring Lord Peter Wimsey.

clue.text: Anti-corrosive coating left off submarine

indicators.note: off means removed, so the letter for left is taken away

parts.note: underseal is a coating that protects a car's underside from rust
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A protective coating has been left off a submarine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Submarine' looks like a noun for the vessel, but it is the adjective meaning beneath the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Submarine as an adjective means existing or happening below the surface of the ocean.
